o: It lies on the side wall of the pelvis lateral to the rectum
Within the parietal pelvic fascia. (Last's p. 399)
Its parasympathetic fibres come from S2, 3 and 4
The pelvic splanchnic nerves. (Last's p. 399)
It measures about 2 cm anteroposteriorly
Nearly 5 cm anteroposteriorly, 2 cm vertically. (Last's p. 399)
All parasympathetic fibres relay in its ganglia
They pass through and relay in the walls of the viscera. (Last's p. 399)

questions.s: Motor supply of the pelvic viscera (Last's):
o: The detrusor is supplied by the pelvic splanchnics
True. The parasympathetic pelvic splanchnic nerves (S2-4) are the motor supply to the detrusor, so they empty the bladder. (Last's p. 399)
The internal urethral sphincter is supplied through the superior hypogastric plexus
Sympathetic. (Last's p. 399)
The internal anal sphincter is supplied by the pelvic splanchnics
By sacral sympathetic ganglia branches through the pelvic plexus. (Last's p. 399)
Pain from the uterine body runs with the pelvic splanchnics
With the hypogastric nerves to T10-L1; lower cervix pain runs with the parasympathetics. (Last's p. 399)

questions.s: Parasympathetic and sympathetic roles in the pelvis (Last's):
o: The pelvic splanchnics supply the colon from the splenic flexure distally
True. Pelvic splanchnic fibres run up through the hypogastric plexuses or behind the peritoneum to the hindgut, from the splenic flexure down to the rectum. (Last's p. 399-400)
Sympathetics are motor to the ductus deferens and seminal vesicles
True. Sympathetic fibres contract the ductus deferens, seminal vesicles and prostatic muscle (emission), and the bladder neck sphincter. (Last's p. 399-400)
The descending colon receives sensory supply from pelvic splanchnics
Its sensory supply is sympathetic. (Last's p. 399-400)
Rectal pain is referred to L1 dermatome
To S2-4 (posterior femoral cutaneous), mimicking sciatica. (Last's p. 399-400)
Stretch afferents travel in the pelvic splanchnic nerves
To sacral segments. (Last's p. 382-3)
The detrusor motor centre lies in the medial pontine reticular formation
True. A detrusor motor centre in the medial pontine reticular formation is controlled by a cortical inhibitory centre; reticulospinal fibres descend to the sacral cord. (Last's p. 382-3)
The external sphincter is supplied by the inferior rectal nerve
By the perineal branch of the pudendal nerve. (Last's p. 382-3)
Destruction of the sacral segments causes automatic reflex emptying
It paralyses the detrusor with overflow incontinence; transection above S2 causes automatic emptying. (Last's p. 382-3)
Its apex attaches to the transverse process of L5
True. The ligament is a sideways V whose apex is on the L5 transverse process, with upper and lower bands fanning out to the ilium. (Last's p. 414)
Its upper band gives partial origin to quadratus lumborum
True. The upper band runs to the iliac crest, gives partial origin to quadratus lumborum and is continuous with the lumbar fascia. (Last's p. 414)
Its lower band blends with the dorsal sacroiliac ligament
With the ventral sacroiliac ligament. (Last's p. 414)
Its upper band attaches to the ischial spine
To the iliac crest. (Last's p. 414)
It arises from S2, 3 and 4
True. The pudendal nerve arises from the anterior divisions of S2, 3 and 4. (Last's p. 414)
It lies medial to the pudendal vessels
True. It leaves the pelvis below piriformis, crosses the sacrospinous ligament medial to the internal pudendal vessels and enters the pudendal canal. (Last's p. 414)
The inferior rectal nerve supplies the internal anal sphincter
It supplies the external anal sphincter. (Last's p. 414)
The dorsal nerve of the penis supplies the skin of the dorsum at the root
The ilioinguinal nerve does. (Last's p. 414)
It arises by eight digitations from the lower eight ribs
True. Its upper four slips interdigitate with serratus anterior and its lower four with latissimus dorsi. (Last's p. 414)
Its lower aponeurotic border forms the inguinal ligament
True. Between the anterior superior iliac spine and the pubic tubercle the free lower border of the aponeurosis is rolled in as the inguinal ligament. (Last's p. 414)
Its upper four digitations interdigitate with latissimus dorsi
With serratus anterior; the lower four with latissimus dorsi. (Last's p. 414)
Its posterior muscular border forms the posterior boundary of the lumbar triangle
The anterior boundary. (Last's p. 414)
The internal oblique arises from the lateral two-thirds of the inguinal ligament

True. Internal oblique arises from the lumbar fascia, the anterior two-thirds of the iliac crest and the lateral two-thirds of the inguinal ligament; transversus only from the lateral half. (Last's p. 414)
Below the arcuate line the transversus aponeurosis passes in front of rectus
True. Below the arcuate line all three aponeuroses pass in front of rectus, leaving only transversalis fascia behind it. (Last's p. 414)
Transversus arises from the lateral two-thirds of the inguinal ligament
From the lateral half. (Last's p. 414)
The conjoint tendon attaches to the anterior superior iliac spine
To the pubic crest and pectineal line. (Last's p. 414)
Pyramidalis is supplied by T12
True. Pyramidalis and the lowest part of rectus are supplied by the subcostal nerve (T12). (Last's p. 414)
The nerves run between internal oblique and transversus
True. The lower intercostal and subcostal nerves run forwards in the neurovascular plane between internal oblique and transversus, as in the thorax. (Last's p. 414)
T7 runs obliquely downwards in the sheath
T7 runs upwards just below the costal margin. (Last's p. 414)
The ilioinguinal nerve enters the inguinal canal through the deep ring
It enters from the side. (Last's p. 414)
The genital branch of genitofemoral supplies cremaster
True. The genital branch passes through the deep ring into the cord coverings and is motor to cremaster and sensory to the spermatic fasciae. (Last's p. 414)
The ilioinguinal is sensory only within the canal
True. Its motor fibres to internal oblique and transversus leave before it enters the canal, so injury in the canal does not weaken the conjoint tendon. (Last's p. 414)
Damage to the ilioinguinal nerve in the canal weakens the conjoint tendon
Its motor branch arises before the canal. (Last's p. 414)
The testis has parasympathetic supply from the vagus
Sympathetic only, mainly T10. (Last's p. 414)

questions.s: Innervation of the peritoneum and gut (Last's):
o: Central diaphragmatic peritoneum is supplied by the phrenic nerve
True. The central diaphragmatic peritoneum is supplied by the phrenic nerve (C3-5), so pain here is referred to the shoulder tip; the periphery is supplied by intercostal nerves. (Last's p. 414)
The obturator nerve is the chief supply of pelvic parietal peritoneum
True. The obturator nerve is the chief supply of pelvic parietal peritoneum, so pelvic peritonitis may refer pain to the medial thigh. (Last's p. 414)
Meissner's plexus lies between the muscle layers
That is Auerbach's; Meissner's is submucosal. (Last's p. 414)
Highly selective vagotomy cuts the nerves to the pylorus
It cuts only branches to fundus and body. (Last's p. 414)
The genitofemoral nerve emerges from its anterior surface
True. The genitofemoral nerve is the only branch to emerge from the anterior surface of psoas; the obturator and lumbosacral trunk emerge medially, the rest laterally. (Last's p. 414)
The obturator nerve emerges from its medial border
With the lumbosacral trunk. (Last's p. 414)
The femoral nerve emerges from its medial border
Its lateral border. (Last's p. 414)
It is supplied mainly by L4
By L1-3, mainly L2. (Last's p. 414)

questions.s: Quadratus lumborum and the lumbar fascia (Last's):
o: Quadratus lumborum lies in the anterior compartment of the lumbar fascia
True. The anterior and middle layers of the lumbar fascia enclose quadratus lumborum; erector spinae lies in the posterior compartment. (Last's p. 414)
The middle layer attaches to the tips of the lumbar transverse processes
True. The middle layer attaches to the tips of the lumbar transverse processes; the anterior layer to their bases. (Last's p. 414)
Psoas minor is present in about 90% of people
In about two-thirds. (Last's p. 414)
The psoas fascia is part of the lumbar fascia
It is not, though its edge blends with the anterior layer. (Last's p. 414)
It passes beneath the lateral arcuate ligament
True. The subcostal nerve and vessels leave the thorax behind the lateral arcuate ligament and run along the 12th rib in front of quadratus lumborum. (Last's p. 360)
It lies behind the kidney
With the iliohypogastric and ilioinguinal nerves. (Last's p. 360)
The nerve lies above the vessels
Below them. (Last's p. 360)
The adrenal cortex arises from neural crest
From intermediate mesoderm; the medulla is neural crest. (Last's p. 360)

questions.s: The fascia of the pelvic wall (Last's):
o: It covers obturator internus and piriformis
True. The parietal pelvic fascia covers obturator internus and piriformis and is firmly attached to the periosteum at their margins. (Last's p. 360)
The sacral plexus lies behind it
Between it and piriformis. (Last's p. 360)
Pelvic nerves lie inside the fascia and vessels outside it
Nerves lie external; vessels internal. (Last's p. 360)
Sacral plexus branches to the buttock pierce the fascia
They do not pierce it. (Last's p. 360)
